name: Muir
positioning: Muir, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Halifax: an art-filled hotel at the centre of the Halifax waterfront in the new Queen's Marque district
best_for: Travelers who want a downtown Halifax base right on the harbour
Guests interested in local art and getting out on the water

facts.text: Muir is at the centre of the Halifax waterfront, in the heart of the new Queen's Marque district.
The Queen's Marque district offers access to the Atlantic Ocean and a multi-million-dollar public art collection.
Scheduled excursions on Reach, the hotel's high-speed 24-foot motorboat, explore the bays and coves of Halifax's historic harbour.
Kayaks and bicycles are available to make use of the hotel's direct water access.
True Colours, the private guest art gallery, hosts regular gallery talks and intimate events.
Guests find a significant collection of local and global art throughout the hotel.
Rooms have furniture and lighting designed and crafted in Canada, curved white oak walls and walnut-panelled flooring.
Rooms have triple-paned soundproofed windows with bedside-controlled blackout drapes.
The Shannon and Thrumcap Suites were designed by Canada's Studio Munge and include a living room and dining area.
Drift serves modern, elevated takes on classic Atlantic Canadian dishes.
Muir offers car and driver service with a hybrid Range Rover.

highlights.text: Little Wing, Muir's 36-foot Morris yacht, gives guests a view of the coastline from the water.
The Watch, the presidential suite, juts over Halifax harbour with ocean views on three sides.
True Colours is a private art gallery for hotel guests with a rotating collection of exhibits.
Windward Wellness includes a fitness centre, spin and yoga studio, exercise classes, vitality spa pool, cold plunge pool, halotherapy salt room, eucalyptus steam room and infrared sauna.
All rooms and suites feature Aesop bath products, custom-made furnishings, original Nova Scotia landscape paintings and ceramics, and a handcrafted walnut bar.

considerations.text: Rollaway beds are not permitted, and the largest-occupancy room, the Signature Double Queen, sleeps a maximum of three.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may not suit guests seeking a secluded retreat.
